raw_output: {"rationale":"Iteration 0 has no Geometry Race Data and no Integration Feedback yet, so this proposal is a neutral, well-bounded baseline chosen from the contract, not a tuned design. Sensor footprint 0.012 m is about half the 25 mm tape width, so a sensor sees a clear fraction of the tape as the robot drifts, without the 0.016 m footprint blurring the edge. Five sensors at 0.015 m spacing (x = -0.03 to +0.03) span about 1.2 times the tape width, so at least one or two sensors read partial tape at any lateral offset up to about 0.04 m, which keeps the signal from dropping out before the 0.06 m off-track limit. Placing the row at y = +0.05 m, ahead of the axle, gives the controller earlier warning of bends than a row level with the axle would. Wheel track 0.12 m and wheel radius 0.03 m are mid-range: a moderate track keeps turn authority reasonable without making the yaw response twitchy. Body width 0.12 m gives an off-track limit of max(0.06, 0.0125 + 0.03) = 0.06 m, so the body width does not widen the allowed excursion yet. Body length 0.18 m and mass 0.8 kg are mid-range values that keep yaw inertia moderate (about 0.8 * (0.18^2 + 0.12^2) / 12 ≈ 0.0029 kg·m²), which should limit oscillation. I expect the baseline to complete the tracks if the controller can hold the line at about 1.5 m/s, and the main risks are line loss on the tighter slalom bends and wheel slip at speed.
